Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — context length / KV cache sizing

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move toward a committed Dedicated capacity plan tied to our Azura EHR summarization product (deal AZR-2026-114). Before we lock term and SKUs, we need a more concrete GPU fleet sizing recommendation that accounts for:

- Model options: we plan to pilot 13B and 70B family open models (we're evaluating a 13B faster path and a 70B for higher-fidelity cases).
- Context: average 32k tokens per session, with worst-case 64k tokens for certain long-patient histories.
- Workload: steady-state 120 concurrent active sessions (interactive summarization), p95 latency target <600ms for the 13B tier and <1s for the 70B tier.
- Quality/cost tradeoffs: teams are open to 4-bit (Q4) quantization for the 70B but want to understand tradeoffs impacting KV cache, memory, and effective QPS.

Can you provide a sizing estimate (GPUs by type, memory footprints after quantization and KV cache for the chosen context lengths), and a short note on how quantization choices affect autoscaling behavior and fallback policies? Also attach any spreadsheet you used.

Appreciate a rapid turnaround as procurement would like numbers for the SOW next week.

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear requirements. Looping in Marcus (serving runtime) and Neha (solutions) — they have the detailed memory math and a sizing spreadsheet I attached (AZR_dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx). High-level summary below; I kept it conservative to meet your latency SLOs and to allow headroom for autoscaling/burst.

Summary (steady-state 120 concurrent sessions split 70/30 between 13B and 70B):
- 13B (int8 / aggressive CPU offload): target GPU: NVIDIA A10G or A16 class (24–48GB), per-GPU footprint ~20–28GB including KV cache for 32k context; KV cache scales roughly linearly with context (32k -> ~8–10GB KV, 64k -> ~16–20GB). For 13B: plan 12 GPUs to reach p95 <600ms with batching & small prefix caching (assumes batching of 6–8).
- 70B (Q4_0 / Q4_KM scenarios): recommended GPU: H100 80GB or H100S 80GB (or 2x 48GB A40 with model sharding). With 4-bit quantization we estimate model weights ~35–45GB; KV cache for 64k context adds 25–30GB depending on sequence distribution. For 70B: plan 18 GPUs (H100 80GB) for the 120 concurrent sessions p95 <1s with conservative batching. If you opt for int8 or mixed-precision, the per-model memory goes up and costs increase.

Key notes on quantization impact and autoscaling:
- Quantization reduces weight memory but KV cache is independent and often dominates for very long contexts; at 64k you should expect KV cache to be ~40–50% of total runtime memory for 70B even with Q4.
- Autoscaling: with aggressive quantization you can pack more model replicas per GPU but warm-up and OOM risk increases during bursty traffic. Suggest conservative overprovisioning of ~15% for traffic spikes or enabling cross-region fallback to hosted endpoints as an emergency policy.
- Fallbacks: we recommend a 3-tier fallback: (1) lighter quantized replica of same model, (2) smaller architecture (13B) with instruction-tuned prompts, (3) hosted API as last-resort. All fallbacks should have deterministic routing so you can track quality regressions.

Attached spreadsheet contains per-model per-GPU memory rows (weights, optimizer state for fine-tuning if needed, KV cache for 8k/32k/64k, recommended replicas, and throughput assumptions). We can convert this into an SOW line-items table for procurement.

Marcus / Neha — can you add any further breakdown (per-token KV bytes assumptions and batching tradeoffs)?

Next steps:
- We can run a short on-prem benchmark with your sample dataset to validate the KV profile (1–2 days).
- If Azura is comfortable, we’ll draft a Dedicated capacity SOW with the two capacity tiers and optional burst pool.

Hi all —

Adding the technical breakdown requested. I pulled the numbers from our benchmark curves and conservative KV sizing assumptions (we assume 32 bytes per KV entry per token for the attention state for these families; that scales with head count but this is a useful rule-of-thumb for sizing).

Per-GPU memory (approx, includes model weights after quantization + KV cache + runtime / scheduler overhead):
- 13B model (int8)
  - 8k context: 12–14 GB total
  - 32k context: 20–28 GB total (KV cache ~8–10 GB)
  - 64k context: 36–40 GB total (KV cache ~22–24 GB)
- 70B model (Q4_KM style 4-bit)
  - 8k context: 38–44 GB total
  - 32k context: 65–75 GB total (KV cache ~22–25 GB)
  - 64k context: 90–110 GB total (KV cache ~45–50 GB)

Fleet sizing rationale for your traffic (120 concurrent):
- If 70/30 split (13B/70B) as Priya estimated, and assuming average request length and effective batching: allocate ~12 x A16 (24GB) for the 13B tier and 18 x H100 80GB for the 70B tier. The H100 numbers assume single-replica per GPU for 70B at 64k; if you require hot-standbys or faster failover add +3 GPUs.

Quantization operational notes:
- Q4 reduces weight footprint ~3–3.5x vs fp16, but KV cache remains roughly the same size (dependent on implementation). So quantization hits model weight component but not KV.
- Memory fragmentation: packing many quantized models into a single GPU can create fragmentation; we recommend per-node padding and smaller replica granularity to prevent OOMs.
- Performance: 4-bit kernels are very fast on H100; on older Ampere-class GPUs the benefit may be less predictable.

Bottlenecks and mitigation:
- KV-IO during long-context serving can be a CPU/RAM bottleneck if you do on-host caching. We recommend GPU-resident KV where latency matters or a fast NVMe-backed shared cache for intermediate designs.

I can run a focused benchmark (with your sample traces) to get exact p95 numbers and tune batch sizes. If Azura can share a 1-hour representative trace (anonymized), we’ll run it in our staging Dedicated cluster and return a validated sheet.
